prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — first a couple quick questions so I recommend the right kind of broker:

- What type of coverage do you need? (Individual/family on the ACA/marketplace, short‑term, COBRA, small‑group/employer, Medicare/Medicare Advantage/Part D)
- What ZIP code or part of Kansas City are you in or prefer (MO or KS)?
- Any other preferences (in‑person meeting, Spanish language, limited budget, certain carriers)?

If you want a quick answer now: there’s no single “best” broker for everyone — the best broker for you depends on the plan type, your budget, whether you want in‑person help, and whether you need Medicare expertise. Below are practical steps and tips to find a strong local broker plus what to ask.

How to find reputable brokers in Kansas City
- Use official directories: NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) agent finder and Medicare.gov (for Medicare agents/counselors). The Kansas Insurance Department can confirm licensing and complaints.
- Search local reviews (Google, Yelp, BBB) and look for brokers with multiple recent positive reviews mentioning ACA or Medicare help, as applicable.
- Ask friends/co‑workers in KC for referrals, especially if they have needs similar to yours.

What to look for in a broker
- Proper license in Missouri or Kansas (ask to see their license number).
- Experience with your plan type (ACA marketplace vs Medicare vs small group).
- Independent vs captive: independent brokers represent multiple carriers (usually better for comparison). Captive agents sell only one carrier’s plans.
- Transparency about compensation (commission vs fee) and whether they’ll include all available plans in your area.
- Willingness to provide a side‑by‑side comparison and explain total expected costs (premium, deductible, out‑of‑pocket max, networks, drug formularies).

Questions to ask a broker before hiring
- Are you licensed in Kansas and/or Missouri? How long have you been doing this?
- Which insurers do you represent? Will you show me every plan available in my area?
- How are you paid (commission, fee)? Will costs to me differ depending on plan?
- Can you help with enrollment, claim issues, and renewals each year?
- Do you have references or client testimonials?

Red flags
- Pushy about one plan/one company and won’t compare alternatives.
- Refuses to disclose license or compensation.
- Poor or no reviews and no willingness to explain coverage differences.

Free counseling for Medicare
- If you’re asking about Medicare, use your State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) for free, unbiased counseling (search “Kansas SHIP” or use Medicare.gov to find local SHIP contact).

If you want, give me your ZIP code and the type of coverage you need and I’ll pull together a short list of well‑rated local brokers/agencies and suggested questions to ask each.
